examples.ko: 수족관에서 커다란 가오리가 천천히 헤엄치고 있었어요.
examples.en: A huge ray was swimming slowly in the aquarium.
A ray has a flat body, so it looks like a diamond shape.

examples.ko: 아이는 가오리를 직접 만져 보고 신기해했어요.
examples.en: The child touched a ray for himself and was amazed.
On the weekend, I flew a ray-shaped kite in the park with my child.

examples.ko: 바다 속에서 가오리 한 마리가 날개를 펄럭이듯 지나갔어요.
examples.en: Under the sea, a ray passed by as if flapping its wings.

examples.ko: 가오리와 상어는 둘 다 뼈가 물렁뼈인 물고기예요.
examples.en: Rays and sharks are both fish whose skeletons are made of cartilage.

explain: 몸이 납작하고 넓은 지느러미가 있는 물고기로, 홍어와 비슷하게 생겼지만 다른 물고기예요. '가오리연'은 이 물고기 모양을 닮은 연을 말해요. 수족관이나 바다 이야기에서 만나기 쉬운 말이에요.

phrases.en: We flew a stingray kite at the beach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가오리 모양을 닮은 연이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A kite shaped like a stingray.

phrases.en: I bought one ray at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물고기는 '마리'로 세므로 수를 말할 때 이렇게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fish are counted with 마리, so this is how to give a number.

phrases.en: I saw a school of rays under the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 마리가 함께 있을 때 '떼'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 떼 for a group of them together.

explain_en: It is a flat fish with broad fins and looks similar to a skate (홍어), but it is a different fish. '가오리연' is a kite shaped like this fish. It is a word you are likely to meet when talking about aquariums or the sea.

examples.ko: 마을 입구에 오래된 거목이 서 있어요.
examples.en: An old giant tree stands at the entrance of the village.
He is a giant of the Korean literary world.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 길가의 거목 한 그루가 쓰러졌어요.
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, a huge roadside tree fell.
I rested for a moment in the shade of the big tree.
They say this giant tree has lived for hundreds of years.
That politician is called a giant of the party.

explain: '큰 나무'는 일상 말이고, 거목은 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요. 비유로는 한 분야를 오래 이끌어 존경받는 원로에게 '문학계의 거목', '정계의 거목'이라고 해요. '거장'이 뛰어난 솜씨에 초점이 있다면, 거목은 영향력과 연륜이 큰 사람에 가까워요.

phrases.en: He is called a giant of the literary world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 분야를 이끈 존경받는 원로를 비유할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for a respected elder who has led a field.

phrases.en: The small seed grew into a giant tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무나 사람이 크게 자랐다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a tree or a person who has grown big.

phrases.en: I rested for a while under a big tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거목'의 일상적인 말이라 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday word for 거목, more common in conversation.

explain_en: '큰 나무' is the everyday phrase, while 거목 appears more in writing and news. Figuratively, a respected elder who led a field for many years is called a '문학계의 거목' or '정계의 거목'. Where '거장' focuses on outstanding skill, 거목 leans toward great influence and long standing.

examples.en: There are many short shrubs in the garden.

examples.ko: 관목은 줄기가 여러 개로 갈라져 자라요.
examples.en: Shrubs grow with their stems splitting into several branches.
We planted shrubs along the road to make a hedge.
A shrub forest continues along the middle of the mountain.

examples.ko: 이 관목에는 봄에 작은 꽃이 피어요.
examples.en: Small flowers bloom on this shrub in spring.

examples.ko: 겨울에도 관목의 잎이 푸르게 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The shrub's leaves stay green even in winter.

explain: '관목'은 키가 작고 줄기가 여러 갈래로 자라는 나무예요. 반대말은 키가 큰 '교목'이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '나무'나 '덤불'이라고 하고, '관목'은 식물 설명이나 과학 글에서 나와요.

phrases.example: 산길 옆에 관목 숲이 넓게 펼쳐져 있어요.
phrases.en: A wide shrub thicket stretches out beside the mountain path.
phrases.nuance_ko: 키 작은 나무가 모여 있는 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a place where low trees grow together.

phrases.en: We planted shrubs along the fence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정원이나 길가에 나무를 심는 상황에서 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for planting trees in a garden or along a road.

phrases.example: 봄이 되자 관목에 노란 꽃이 피었어요.
phrases.en: When spring came, yellow flowers bloomed on the shrubs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에'를 붙여 식물의 변화를 설명하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the particle 에 to describe a change in a plant.

explain_en: '관목' is a short plant whose stems grow in several branches. Its opposite is the tall tree '교목'. In daily speech people just say '나무' or '덤불', while '관목' appears in plant descriptions and science writing.

en: to be vast; to be extensive

examples.en: Siberia is truly vast.
I can see a field stretching vastly before my eyes.
They say space is far vaster than we imagine.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 땅이 광대해서 지역마다 날씨가 달라요.
examples.en: That country's land is vast, so the weather differs by region.
I've never seen such a vast desert.

examples.ko: 그 공원은 광대할 뿐 아니라 경치도 아름다워요.
examples.en: That park is not only vast but also beautiful.

explain: 땅, 바다, 우주, 지식처럼 범위가 아주 넓을 때 써요. '넓다'보다 웅장한 느낌이고 말보다 글에서 더 자주 나와요. 방이나 길에는 쓰지 않고 '광대한 ~' 모양으로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: They farm on a vast stretch of land.
phrases.nuance_ko: '광대한 ~' 모양으로 명사를 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in the form '광대한 ~' to modify a noun.

phrases.en: The universe is so vast that it has no end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 말할 때 쓰고, 우주나 바다처럼 아주 큰 범위에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite spoken form; fits very large scopes like the universe or the sea.

phrases.en: The grassland stretches out vast before my eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '광대하게'로 동사를 꾸며 넓은 풍경을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form '광대하게' describes a wide landscape spreading out.

explain_en: Use it for land, sea, space, or knowledge with a very wide range. It feels grander than 넓다 and shows up more in writing than speech. It is not used for rooms or roads, and often appears as '광대한 ~'.

examples.ko: 이 생수에는 광물질이 많이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This bottled water contains a lot of minerals.
Minerals are important for bone health.
Plants get minerals from the soil.

examples.ko: 이 화장품에는 광물질 성분이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This cosmetic contains mineral ingredients.

examples.ko: 비타민뿐만 아니라 광물질도 꼭 챙겨 드세요.
examples.en: Make sure to take minerals as well as vitamins.
It's a paint made with color taken from minerals.

explain: 땅이나 돌에서 나오는 무기물을 말해요. 영양 이야기에서는 '미네랄'이라고 더 많이 해요. '광물질'은 설명하는 글이나 수업에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: This hot spring water is rich in minerals.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이나 흙에 광물질이 많을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for water or soil that contains a lot of mineral matter.

phrases.en: I drink water with lots of minerals.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 비슷하지만 영양과 건강 이야기에서는 '미네랄'이 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, but 'mineral' is more common when talking about nutrition and health.

phrases.example: 이 화장품에는 광물질 성분이 들어 있어요.
phrases.en: This cosmetic contains mineral ingredients.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제품 설명에서 무엇으로 만들어졌는지 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in product descriptions to say what something is made of.

explain_en: It refers to inorganic substances that come from the earth or rocks. In talk about nutrition, people more often say '미네랄'. '광물질' appears more in explanatory texts and classes.

examples.ko: 모내기가 끝나고 나서 동칠이는 그 논둑에 콩을 심었어요.
examples.en: After the rice transplanting was over, Dongchil planted beans on that paddy ridge.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 논둑이 미끄러워서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: When it rains, the paddy ridges are slippery, so you have to be careful.
The children played, running along the paddy ridge.
We sat on the paddy ridge and ate a snack.

examples.ko: 논둑길을 걷다 보니 개구리 소리가 크게 들렸어요.
examples.en: As I walked along the path between the paddies, I heard frogs croaking loudly.
The cow climbs up the paddy ridge and grazes on the grass.

explain: 논과 논 사이, 또는 논 가장자리에 흙을 쌓아 만든 둑이에요. '논두렁'이라고도 해요. 시골 풍경이나 옛이야기에서 '논둑길'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I walked slowly along the path on the rice-field ridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 논둑 위에 난 좁은 길을 말해요. 시골 풍경 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A narrow path on a field ridge, often used in countryside scenes.

phrases.en: The children play on the ridges between the fields.
phrases.nuance_ko: '논둑'과 같은 뜻의 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A synonym with the same meaning as '논둑'.

phrases.en: While working, I sat on the ridge and rested.
phrases.nuance_ko: 논 가장자리에 앉아 쉬는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes sitting to rest at the edge of a rice field.
phrases.en_equiv: to sit on the field ridge

explain_en: It is the earthen bank built between rice paddies or along their edges. It is also called '논두렁'. It often appears in country scenery and old stories, as in '논둑길' (the path along the ridge).

examples.ko: 우리는 산 능선을 따라 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: We walked slowly along the mountain ridge.

examples.ko: 능선 위에서 보는 해돋이가 정말 멋있어요.
examples.en: The sunrise seen from the ridge is really beautiful.
When the fog cleared, a distant ridge came into view.

examples.ko: 바람이 센 능선에서는 모자를 꼭 잡아야 해요.
examples.en: On a windy ridge, you have to hold your hat tight.

examples.ko: 저 능선만 넘으면 마을이 나올 거예요.
examples.en: Once we cross that ridge, we'll reach the village.

examples.ko: 이 능선은 길이 좁아서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: The path on this ridge is narrow, so be careful.

explain: 산에서 '산꼭대기'는 제일 높은 한 점이고, '능선'은 그 꼭대기들을 이어 주는 길쭉한 선이에요. 등산 이야기에서 '능선을 타다', '능선을 따라 걷다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: On the weekend I hiked along the ridge with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 등산에서 능선 길을 따라 걷는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In hiking, it means walking along a ridge trail.

phrases.en: It is very windy on the ridge trail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능선 위로 난 길을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the path along the top of a ridge.

phrases.en: When I got up on the ridge, I could see the whole village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼭대기가 아니라 능선 위로 올라갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for climbing up onto the ridge rather than the summit.
phrases.en_equiv: to climb up onto the ridge

explain_en: '산꼭대기' is the single highest point, while 능선 is the long line that connects the peaks. In hiking talk you often hear '능선을 타다' or '능선을 따라 걷다'.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 대부분 늪지대라서 집을 짓기 어려워요.
examples.en: Most of this area is swampland, so it's hard to build houses.

examples.ko: 늪지대에는 희귀한 새와 식물이 많이 살아요.
examples.en: Many rare birds and plants live in the wetlands.

examples.ko: 늪지대를 걸을 때는 발이 빠질 수 있으니 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful when walking through a swamp because your feet can sink.

examples.ko: 우리는 늪지대 생태 체험을 하러 갔어요.
examples.en: We went on an ecological field trip to a swamp.
I got bitten by a lot of mosquitoes in the damp swamp.

examples.ko: 도시가 커지면서 늪지대가 점점 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: As the city grows, the swampland is gradually shrinking.

explain: '늪'이 물이 고여 질척한 땅 하나라면, '늪지대'는 그런 곳이 넓게 이어진 지역이에요. 비슷한 '습지'는 물기가 많은 땅을 더 넓게 가리켜요. '-지대'는 '산악 지대'처럼 다른 말 뒤에 붙는 말이에요.

phrases.en: This is a wetland where many water birds live.
phrases.nuance_ko: '늪지대'보다 물기가 많은 땅을 더 넓게 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word than 늪지대 for any land with a lot of moisture.

phrases.en: We drove through a wide swampland.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기를 말할 때 '넓은'을 붙여서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '넓은' is often added to describe the size.

phrases.en: Alligators live in warm swamps.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이나 식물이 사는 곳을 말할 때 조사 '에'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the particle 에 to say where animals or plants live.

explain_en: While '늪' is a single muddy, water-logged place, '늪지대' is a wide area where such places continue. The similar '습지' refers to wet land more broadly. '-지대' is a suffix that attaches to other words, as in '산악 지대'.

examples.en: I found salamander eggs by the stream.
They say salamanders are often seen in clear valleys.
The child caught a salamander and showed it to me.
The salamander slowly crept into a crack in the rock.
I went to the valley to take photos of salamanders.
Salamanders live in the pond in the forest.

explain: 도마뱀과 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 도롱뇽은 물가에 사는 양서류이고 도마뱀은 파충류예요. 표준어는 '도롱뇽'이고, 맑은 계곡이나 연못 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 계곡 바위 밑에서 도롱뇽 알을 봤어요.
phrases.en: I saw salamander eggs under a rock in the valley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도롱뇽은 물속에 알을 낳아서 '알'과 함께 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Salamanders lay eggs in water, so this pairing is common.

phrases.en: Salamanders live in this valley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도롱뇽이 사는 곳을 소개할 때 '살다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 살다 to say where salamanders live.

phrases.en: I saw a salamander at the forest pond yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '을'을 붙여서 직접 도롱뇽을 만난 경험을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 을, it tells of actually seeing one.

explain_en: People often confuse it with a lizard (도마뱀), but a 도롱뇽 is an amphibian living near water, while a 도마뱀 is a reptile. The standard spelling is '도롱뇽', and it often comes up in talk about clear valleys and ponds.

examples.en: Grasshoppers hop around the rice fields in autumn.
The children are catching grasshoppers.
Grasshoppers live on grass.

examples.ko: 메뚜기 한 마리가 내 어깨에 앉았어요.
examples.en: A grasshopper landed on my shoulder.
I heard people used to eat stir-fried grasshoppers.
Try jumping high like a grasshopper.

explain: 메뚜기는 곤충이지만 예전에는 가을에 볶아서 반찬으로 먹기도 했어요. 비슷하게 풀밭에서 보이는 곤충으로 방아깨비가 있고, 가을밤에 우는 곤충은 귀뚜라미예요.

phrases.en: A grasshopper jumps high in the grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 메뚜기의 가장 특징적인 움직임을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the grasshopper's most characteristic movement.

phrases.en: As a child, I caught grasshoppers in the rice field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곤충을 잡는 놀이를 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about catching insects as play.

phrases.example: 풀잎 위에 메뚜기 한 마리가 앉아 있어요.
phrases.en: A grasshopper is sitting on a blade of grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곤충은 '마리'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Insects are counted with 마리.

explain_en: 메뚜기 is an insect, but people used to stir-fry it as a side dish in autumn. Another insect seen in grass is the 방아깨비, while the one that sings on autumn nights is the 귀뚜라미.

examples.en: In spring, I planted an apple tree sapling in the yard.

examples.ko: 시장에서 묘목 한 그루에 얼마인지 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I asked at the market how much one sapling cost.

examples.ko: 묘목이 잘 자라도록 물을 자주 줘요.
examples.en: I water the sapling often so that it grows well.

examples.ko: 묘목은 키가 작아서 바람에 쉽게 꺾여요.
examples.en: Saplings are short, so they snap easily in the wind.

examples.ko: 식목일에 학교에서 묘목 나누어 주기 행사를 했어요.
examples.en: On Arbor Day, my school held an event giving out saplings.
Please put a fence around the young sapling.

explain: 옮겨 심으려고 키운 어린 나무를 말해요. 이미 크게 자란 것은 그냥 '나무'라고 하고, 묘목을 셀 때는 '그루'를 써서 '묘목 세 그루'라고 해요. 보통 묘목은 가게나 시장에서 사요.

phrases.en: I planted saplings with my family on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어린 나무를 땅에 옮겨 심을 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for planting young trees.

phrases.en: I bought three persimmon tree saplings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무를 세는 단위 '그루'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the counter 그루, which is for trees.

phrases.en: In spring I buy saplings at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 묘목은 보통 가게나 시장에서 산다는 것을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows that saplings are usually bought at shops or markets.

explain_en: It means a young tree grown to be transplanted. A fully grown one is simply a '나무', and saplings are counted with '그루', as in '묘목 세 그루'. People usually buy saplings at nurseries or markets.

examples.en: A jellyfish is an invertebrate.
Insects and shellfish are among the invertebrates.
In science class, we tried classifying invertebrates.
Octopuses are invertebrates too.
I watched a video observing invertebrates under the sea.

examples.ko: 무척추동물은 척추 대신 껍데기가 있는 경우도 있어요.
examples.en: Some invertebrates have a shell instead of a backbone.

explain: 반대말은 '척추동물'이에요. 곤충, 조개, 오징어, 해파리처럼 등뼈가 없는 동물을 묶어 부르는 과학 용어라서 수업이나 책에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Invertebrates and vertebrates have different body structures.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지를 비교할 때 짝으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as a pair when comparing the two.

phrases.en: Squid belong to the invertebrates.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 동물이 이 무리에 들어간다고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain that an animal belongs to this group.

phrases.en: That scientist studies marine invertebrates.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학 수업이나 글에서 자주 나오는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common usage in science classes and texts.

explain_en: Its counterpart is '척추동물' (vertebrate). It is a science term grouping animals without a backbone, like insects, clams, squid and jellyfish, so it comes up often in class and books.

examples.en: Yellow dandelions have bloomed by the roadside.
Dandelion seeds fly away in the wind.
My grandmother made dandelion greens for me.
I picked a dandelion on the lawn.
When spring comes, dandelions appear everywhere.
I want to live tenaciously like a dandelion.

explain: 하얗게 둥근 씨앗 뭉치는 '민들레 홀씨'라고 해요. 아무 데서나 잘 자라서 동요나 시에서는 끈질기게 사는 사람을 민들레에 비유해요. 잎은 나물로도 먹어요.

phrases.example: 봄이 되면 길가에 노란 민들레가 많이 피어요.
phrases.en: In spring, many yellow dandelions bloom by the roadside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 민들레 꽃의 색을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used to describe the color of the flower.

phrases.en: The child blew on the dandelion seeds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 지고 난 뒤 하얗게 둥근 씨앗 뭉치를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the round white seed puff after the flower fades.

phrases.en: Dandelions have bloomed in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 필 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for dandelions blooming.

explain_en: The round white puff of seeds is called '민들레 홀씨'. Because it grows almost anywhere, children's songs and poems compare tough, persistent people to a dandelion. The leaves are also eaten as '나물'.

examples.en: On this farm, they let the cows graze on the mountain.

examples.ko: 양을 풀밭에 방목하면 고기 맛이 좋아진대요.
examples.en: They say the meat tastes better if sheep are let out to graze on pasture.
In winter, we keep them in pens instead of letting them graze.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 우리 부모님은 저를 거의 방목하다시피 키우셨어요.
examples.en: When I was little, my parents raised me almost hands-off.

examples.ko: 닭을 마당에 방목했더니 벌레를 잘 잡아요.
examples.en: Since I let the chickens roam in the yard, they catch bugs well.

examples.ko: 여름 동안 말을 초원에 방목할 계획이에요.
examples.en: I plan to let the horses graze on the grassland for the summer.

explain: 가축을 우리 밖 풀밭에 풀어 놓고 키운다는 뜻이고 '소를 방목하다'처럼 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 아이나 직원을 간섭하지 않고 자유롭게 내버려 둔다는 비유가 돼요. 이때는 약간 농담처럼 들리기도 해요.

phrases.en: My parents raised me with a very free hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이에게 간섭이나 관리를 거의 하지 않고 자유롭게 자라게 한다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor for raising a child with almost no supervision or interference.

explain_en: It means letting livestock roam on open pasture, as in '소를 방목하다'. Used about people, it becomes a metaphor for leaving a child or employee free without interfering, and it can sound a little jokey.

examples.en: The autumn mountains have started to turn patchy red.

examples.ko: 모기에 물려서 팔에 불긋불긋 자국이 생겼어요.
examples.en: I got bitten by mosquitoes and red marks appeared here and there on my arm.
Red leaves dot the view outside the window, and it's pretty.

examples.ko: 얼굴에 불긋불긋 뭐가 났는데 병원에 가야 할까요?
examples.en: Red spots have come up on my face. Should I go to the hospital?

examples.ko: 저녁 하늘이 불긋불긋 변하는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the evening sky turn patchy red.

examples.ko: 꽃이 불긋불긋 피어 있는 길을 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked down a path where red flowers were blooming here and there.

explain: 붉은 점이나 무늬가 군데군데 있는 모습이에요. 여러 색이 섞여 화려할 때는 '울긋불긋'을 써요. '단풍이 불긋불긋 물들다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: Reddish marks were left on my arm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 형태로 바꿔서 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form used to describe a noun.

phrases.en: The mountain turned colorful with autumn leaves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붉은색만이 아니라 여러 색이 섞여 화려할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when many colors mix colorfully, not only red.

phrases.en: Red spots appeared here and there on my neck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붉은 점이 여기저기 있는 모습을 쉽게 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to describe red spots scattered here and there.

explain_en: It describes red spots or patches here and there. When several colors mix and look vivid, use '울긋불긋' instead. A typical use is '단풍이 불긋불긋 물들다'.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 돌아온 고향 산천이 낯설게 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: The hometown scenery I came back to after a long time felt unfamiliar.
Autumn colors have spread over all the hills and streams.
The landscape is the same, but the people have changed a lot.

examples.ko: 우리나라 산천을 두루 돌아다니며 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I traveled around Korea's landscapes taking photos.
I took a train to see the countryside scenery.
I read a poem that sang of the beauty of the mountains and rivers.

explain: '고향 산천'처럼 산과 내가 있는 자연 풍경, 특히 정든 고향을 따뜻하게 말할 때 써요. 노래나 시, 글에서 많이 나오고 일상 대화에서는 조금 옛스럽게 들려요. '강산'이나 '금수강산'과도 비슷하게 쓰여요.

phrases.en: They say even the mountains and rivers change in ten years.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산천'과 비슷하게 자연 풍경을 뜻하고, 이 속담 같은 표현에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '산천' in meaning nature scenery, and often seen in this proverb.

phrases.en: The mountains and streams here are really beautiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자연 풍경이 좋다고 칭찬할 때 쓰는 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sentence for praising beautiful natural scenery.

phrases.en: While traveling, I looked around the mountains and streams of our country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자연을 천천히 구경한다는 느낌이 있는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase with the feel of slowly taking in nature.

explain_en: It is used for natural scenery with mountains and streams, especially to speak warmly of a beloved hometown, as in '고향 산천'. It appears a lot in songs, poems and writing, and sounds a bit old-fashioned in everyday talk. It is used similarly to '강산' and '금수강산'.

examples.en: There is one pistil in the middle of the flower.
I compared the shapes of the pistil and stamens.
Bees carry pollen to the pistil.

examples.ko: 암술 끝에 꽃가루가 붙으면 열매를 맺어요.
examples.en: When pollen sticks to the tip of the pistil, the plant bears fruit.

examples.ko: 이 꽃은 암술이 길고 수술이 짧아요.
examples.en: In this flower, the pistil is long and the stamens are short.
In science class I drew a pistil.

explain: 꽃의 가운데에서 열매와 씨를 만드는 쪽을 말해요. 꽃가루를 만드는 '수술'과 짝으로 외우면 쉬워요. 주로 과학 수업이나 식물 이야기에서 나와요.

phrases.example: 암술과 수술은 꽃에서 하는 일이 달라요.
phrases.en: The pistil and the stamen have different roles in a flower.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학 수업에서 짝으로 같이 외우는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Learned as a pair in science class.

phrases.en: When pollen sticks to the stigma, fruit forms.
phrases.nuance_ko: 암술의 맨 위쪽, 꽃가루가 붙는 부분이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The top of the pistil, where pollen sticks.

phrases.example: 이 꽃은 암술이 길어서 눈에 잘 띄어요.
phrases.en: This flower has a long pistil, so it stands out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃의 모양을 설명할 때 '길다/짧다'를 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 길다/짧다 when describing a flower's shape.

explain_en: It is the part at the center of a flower that goes on to form the fruit and seeds. It is easy to remember as a pair with '수술' (stamen), which makes pollen. It mainly appears in science class and talk about plants.

examples.en: The coastal area suffered heavy typhoon damage.

examples.ko: 이 배는 연안을 따라 천천히 움직여요.
examples.en: This ship moves slowly along the coast.
Lots of clams are caught in the coastal waters.

examples.ko: 동해 연안은 경치가 좋아서 여행객이 많아요.
examples.en: The East Sea coast has beautiful scenery, so there are many tourists.

examples.ko: 연안 어업은 작은 배로 하는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Coastal fishing is often done on small boats.
Trash piled up along the shore, so residents cleaned it.

explain: '해안'은 땅과 바다가 만나는 가장자리를 말하고, '연안'은 그 바다와 땅 가까운 지역 전체를 넓게 말해요. 뉴스에서 '연안 지역', '연안 어업'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: The wind blows strongly in the coastal area.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바다와 가까운 땅 전체를 말할 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used often in the news for the whole area near the sea.

phrases.en: Many people work in coastal fishing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먼바다가 아니라 가까운 바다에서 하는 고기잡이를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to fishing done in nearby waters, not the far sea.

phrases.en: Coastal cities have many ports.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바다 가까이에 있는 도시를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to cities located near the sea.

explain_en: '해안' is the edge where land meets sea, while '연안' covers the whole area of sea and land near that edge. News often uses it in '연안 지역' (coastal region) and '연안 어업' (coastal fishing).

examples.en: We humans also belong to the primates, scientifically speaking.
Chimpanzees are the primates closest to humans.
Primates are good at grasping things with their hands.

examples.ko: 동물원에서 아이와 함께 영장류 우리를 구경했어요.
examples.en: At the zoo, I looked at the primate enclosure with my child.
This institute studies the behavior of primates.
Gorillas and monkeys are also classified as primates.

explain: 원숭이, 침팬지, 고릴라, 사람을 한데 묶는 분류 이름이에요. 일상에서는 '원숭이'라고 말하고, '영장류'는 과학 수업이나 뉴스, 설명하는 글에서 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 과학자는 영장류 연구를 오래 했어요.
phrases.en: That scientist has done primate research for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학이나 학문 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in science and academic talk.

phrases.en: Primates live in groups.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '는'을 붙여 영장류 전체의 특징을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle '는', it introduces a general fact about primates.

phrases.en: I saw a monkey at the zoo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이고, '영장류'는 사람까지 묶는 더 넓은 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday word; '영장류' is a broader group name that includes humans.

explain_en: It is the group name that covers monkeys, chimpanzees, gorillas and humans. In daily talk people say '원숭이', while '영장류' appears mostly in science classes, the news and explanatory writing.

en: to be temperate; to be mild

examples.en: Jeju Island is mild even in winter.
Tangerines grow well in a mild climate.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 온난해서 눈이 거의 안 와요.
examples.en: This region is mild, so it hardly ever snows.

examples.ko: 남쪽 바다 근처는 비교적 온난할 거예요.
examples.en: Near the southern sea it should be relatively mild.
Thanks to the mild weather, it was great for a walk.
If the Earth gets warmer, sea levels rise.

explain: '따뜻하다'는 몸, 방, 음식에도 쓰지만 '온난하다'는 날씨, 기후, 지역에만 써요. 일기 예보나 지리 이야기에서 자주 나와요. '지구 온난화'라는 말로 더 자주 들어요.

phrases.example: 이 지역은 온난한 기후라서 살기 좋아요.
phrases.en: This region has a mild climate, so it is nice to live in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 지역의 날씨를 설명하는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before a noun to describe a region's weather.

phrases.en: The southern region is mild even in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장 끝에서 날씨가 따뜻하고 부드럽다고 말하는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite sentence-ending form saying the weather is mild.

phrases.en: This region is not mild in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨가 따뜻하지 않다고 부정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form for saying the weather is not mild.

explain_en: '따뜻하다' works for bodies, rooms, and food, but '온난하다' is only for weather, climate, and regions. It appears in forecasts and geography. You will most often hear it in '지구 온난화'.

examples.en: I heard an owl in the forest at night.
Owls see well even in dark places.
I saw a big owl for the first time at the zoo.

examples.ko: 저는 밤늦게까지 깨어 있는 올빼미 같은 사람이에요.
examples.en: I'm a night owl who stays up late.
The owl's eyes are big and round, so it's cute.

examples.ko: 아이가 올빼미 모양 가방을 갖고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The child wants an owl-shaped bag.

explain: 올빼미는 밤에 활동하는 새예요. 비슷한 '부엉이'는 머리 위에 귀처럼 보이는 깃털이 있는 쪽을 말하는데, 일상에서는 둘을 섞어서 쓰기도 해요. 사람에게는 '올빼미'를 밤늦게까지 깨어 있는 사람으로 비유해요.

phrases.en: I'm a night owl who goes to bed late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밤늦게까지 깨어 있는 사람들을 가볍게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light way to call people who stay up late at night.

phrases.en: An owl's eyes are very big.
phrases.nuance_ko: 올빼미의 눈을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about an owl's eyes.

phrases.example: 나무 위에 올빼미 한 마리가 앉아 있어요.
phrases.en: An owl is sitting on the tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새는 '마리'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Birds are counted with 마리.

explain_en: 올빼미 is a bird that is active at night. The similar 부엉이 refers to owls with ear-like feather tufts on top of the head, though in daily speech people sometimes mix the two. For people, 올빼미 is used figuratively for someone who stays up late.

examples.ko: 우리는 벽을 짙은 색깔로 울긋불긋 꾸몄어요.
examples.en: We decorated the wall in deep colors, all colorful.
When autumn came, the mountains turned a riot of colors.
The children gathered, wearing colorful hanbok.
The flowers in the flower bed are blooming in many colors.
Colorful fruit is piled up in the market.

examples.ko: 설날 거리에 울긋불긋 등이 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: Colorful lanterns are hanging on the streets for the New Year.

explain: 여러 가지 진한 색이 섞여 화려하게 보이는 모습이에요. 단풍, 꽃, 옷, 장식처럼 눈에 확 들어오는 것에 많이 써요. '알록달록'도 비슷한 말로 쓰여요.

phrases.en: The colorful autumn leaves are really pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사 '울긋불긋'을 '울긋불긋한'으로 바꿔 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form used to modify a noun directly.

phrases.en: Flowers have bloomed in bright colors in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 색의 꽃이 화려하게 핀 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes flowers of many colors blooming brilliantly.

phrases.en: The room the kids decorated in bright colors is cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 울긋불긋보다 가볍고 귀여운 느낌이라 아이 물건에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels lighter and cuter than 울긋불긋, fitting children's things well.

explain_en: It describes many strong colors mixed together and looking gorgeous. It is often used for autumn leaves, flowers, clothes and decorations that catch the eye. '알록달록' is a similar word.

examples.en: Oxygen is an element people absolutely need.
I memorized element symbols in science class.

examples.ko: 주기율표에는 백 개가 넘는 원소가 있어요.
examples.en: The periodic table has more than a hundred elements.

examples.ko: 이 물은 어떤 원소로 이루어져 있나요?
examples.en: What elements is this water made of?

examples.ko: 새로운 원소를 발견한 과학자가 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: The scientist who discovered a new element received a prize.

examples.ko: 철은 지구에 많은 원소 중 하나예요.
examples.en: Iron is one of the abundant elements on Earth.

explain: 원소는 화학에서 더 나눌 수 없는 기본 물질을 말해요. 수소, 산소, 철이 원소예요. '요소'와는 달라요. 요소는 어떤 일의 한 부분이에요.

phrases.en: The element symbol for hydrogen is H.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학 시간에 가장 자주 쓰는 합친 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The compound used most often in science class.

phrases.en: Gold is a very precious chemical element.
phrases.nuance_ko: '화학'을 앞에 붙이면 과학에서 말하는 원소라는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 화학 makes it clear that it means an element in science.

phrases.example: 물은 수소와 산소 두 원소로 이루어져 있어요.
phrases.en: Water is made of two elements, hydrogen and oxygen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 물질이 무엇으로 되어 있는지 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain what a substance is made of.

explain_en: 원소 is a basic substance in chemistry that cannot be broken down further by chemical means. Hydrogen, oxygen and iron are elements. It differs from 요소, which means a part or factor of something.

examples.en: Most of the air is nitrogen.
Snack bags are filled with nitrogen.
Plants definitely need nitrogen.
We learned about nitrogen in science class.
Liquid nitrogen is extremely cold.
Fertilizer has a lot of nitrogen in it.

explain: 한국 과자 봉지는 늘 빵빵한데, 그 안의 기체가 '질소'예요. 그래서 '질소 과자'라고 포장만 크고 과자는 적을 때 농담처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 질소 과자는 봉지만 크고 과자가 적어요.
phrases.en: Nitrogen snacks have a big bag but few snacks inside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포장만 크고 내용물이 적은 과자를 농담처럼 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A joking name for snacks with a big bag but little inside.

phrases.example: 봉지 안에 질소 가스가 들어 있어요.
phrases.en: There is nitrogen gas inside the bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기체 상태의 질소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about nitrogen as a gas.

phrases.en: Nitrogen is the most abundant gas in the air.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학 이야기에서 공기의 성분을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in science talk about what air is made of.

explain_en: Korean snack bags are always puffed up, and the gas inside is 질소. So people joke about '질소 과자' when the bag is big but there is little snack inside.

examples.ko: 여름 방학에 곤충을 채집하러 산에 갔어요.
examples.en: During summer vacation, I went to the mountain to collect insects.
The kids gather shellfish at the beach.

examples.ko: 식물을 채집할 때는 뿌리가 다치지 않게 조심해요.
examples.en: When collecting plants, I take care not to hurt the roots.
The teacher told us to collect leaves and bring them.
The research team collected river water and tested its quality.

examples.ko: 허락 없이 채집하면 안 되는 식물도 있어요.
examples.en: There are also plants you must not collect without permission.

explain: 곤충, 식물, 조개, 물처럼 자연에 있는 것을 관찰이나 연구를 위해 모을 때 써요. 우표나 자료를 모으는 건 '수집하다'라고 하고, 일상에서는 '캐다', '잡다'처럼 구체적으로 말하는 경우도 많아요.

phrases.en: I did insect collecting as my vacation homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 '채집하다'의 명사형 '채집'과 함께 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing using '채집', the noun form of '채집하다'.

phrases.en: The children collected leaves in the forest and brought them back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모아서 가지고 돌아온다는 뜻의 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connected form meaning to collect something and bring it back.

phrases.example: 이 바닷가에서는 조개를 채집할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can collect shellfish on this beach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그곳에서 모을 수 있다고 가능성을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that collecting is possible in a place.

explain_en: It is used for gathering things found in nature, such as insects, plants, shellfish or water, for observation or research. Collecting stamps or data is '수집하다', and in daily talk people often use more specific verbs like '캐다' or '잡다'.

dis.h: gather plants or insects in the wild

p.n: 수집하다 sounds like building a collection; 채집하다 stresses gathering in nature.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 철광석 수출로 많은 돈을 벌어요.
examples.en: This country earns a lot of money from exporting iron ore.

examples.ko: 철광석을 높은 열로 녹여서 철을 만들어요.
examples.en: Iron is made by melting iron ore at high heat.
Steel mills bring in iron ore by ship.

examples.ko: 철광석 가격이 오르면 자동차 값도 영향을 받아요.
examples.en: When the price of iron ore rises, car prices are affected too.

examples.ko: 철광석이 많이 나는 산에는 광산이 있어요.
examples.en: The mountain where a lot of iron ore is found has a mine.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 철광석 표본을 직접 봤어요.
examples.en: In class I saw an iron ore specimen in person.

explain: '구리 광석'처럼 '광석' 앞에 금속 이름을 붙여 말해요. 철광석은 석탄과 함께 제철 이야기에 같이 나오고, 뉴스에서는 '철광석 가격'처럼 경제 소식에도 나와요.

phrases.en: Miners dig iron ore from the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광석을 땅에서 파낼 때 '캐다'를 짝으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb 캐다 pairs with ore when digging it from the ground.

phrases.example: 철광석 가격이 올라서 철강 회사가 걱정해요.
phrases.en: Iron ore prices went up, so steel companies are worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경제 뉴스에서 자주 듣는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression often heard in economic news.

phrases.example: 이 지역에는 큰 철광석 광산이 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a big iron ore mine in this region.
phrases.nuance_ko: 철광석을 캐내는 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the place where iron ore is mined.

explain_en: You put a metal's name before '광석' (ore), like '구리 광석' (copper ore). 철광석 often appears together with coal in talk about steelmaking, and in the news it shows up in economic reports like '철광석 가격' (iron ore prices).

examples.en: The solar system has eight planets.
They say an object from outside the solar system was found.
In elementary school, I made a model of the solar system.

examples.ko: 지구는 태양계에서 태양과 세 번째로 가까워요.
examples.en: Earth is the third closest to the sun in the solar system.
I wonder where the edge of the solar system is.

examples.ko: 태양계 그림을 보고 행성 이름을 외웠어요.
examples.en: I memorized the planets' names by looking at a picture of the solar system.

explain: 범위로 보면 우주 > 은하 > 태양계 > 지구 순서로 작아져요. 태양계는 우리 해를 중심으로 한 범위만 가리켜서 우주 전체와는 달라요. 보통 '태양계 행성', '태양계 밖'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I memorized the names of the solar system planets in order.
phrases.nuance_ko: 태양 주위를 도는 행성을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for planets orbiting the sun.

phrases.en: The sun is the center of the solar system.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'를 붙여 태양계에 속한 것이나 성질을 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '의' describes something belonging to the solar system.

phrases.example: 지구는 태양계 안에서 세 번째 행성이에요.
phrases.en: Earth is the third planet in the solar system.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밖'과 반대로 태양계 범위 안을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 'outside', meaning within the solar system.

explain_en: By scale it shrinks in the order 우주 > 은하 > 태양계 > 지구. 태양계 covers only the area around our sun, so it is not the same as the whole universe. It is usually used as 태양계 행성 or 태양계 밖.

examples.en: We passed through a boundless plain by train.
Mongolia has many wide plains.
A herd of horses galloped across the plain.
The sunset seen from the plain is really beautiful.
I want to visit the North American plains.
Plains are good for farming.

explain: 산이 거의 없이 넓고 평평한 땅이에요. '평야'와 비슷한 말이고, '평원'은 탁 트인 넓은 풍경을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 이 지역은 평야가 넓어서 쌀농사가 잘돼요.
phrases.en: This area has wide plains, so rice farming goes well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '평원'과 비슷한 말인데 농사짓는 넓은 들을 말할 때 더 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '평원', but fits better for wide farmland.

phrases.en: Horses are running across the wide plain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탁 트인 풍경을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when describing an open landscape.

phrases.en: The train runs across the plain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이동하는 장면을 말할 때 붙여 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for describing movement through the landscape.

explain_en: It is wide, flat land with almost no mountains. It is close to '평야', and '평원' suits descriptions of open, far-reaching scenery.
